subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals & term options
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@finapps.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, AWS Marketplace AM <aws-am@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals & term options

Hi Nina —

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed, I’m following up with a concise summary of the private offer options so your procurement and finance teams can review quickly. I’ve attached a term sheet and a simple pricing grid that contrasts annual vs 36-month commitments. High-level options: 

- 12-month term, standard seat/usage rates, eligible for standard AWS settlement cadence
- 36-month term, deeper unit discount and ability to amortize over longer commitment (preferred by finance)
- Volume tiers that reduce per-token unit price once monthly committed usage thresholds are hit

Key buyer approval questions I heard you flag: 
1) Does a 36-month PO require additional legal signoff from Redwood beyond our standard AWS private offer paperwork?
2) Can we escalate the buyer approval flow in AWS so the contract doesn’t stall at procurement for more than 10 business days?
3) Are there pricing floors for shorter notice terminations?

Sergio and Karthik — looping you in to confirm what we need from our side for a 36-month private offer and suggested language for the buyer’s PO to keep approval timelines short. 

Action items proposed:
- I’ll share a one-page summary the buyer can hand to procurement (attached).
- Karthik to confirm internal legal/ops signoff steps for >24 month private offers.
- Nina — if you can share the procurement contact and any approval tier thresholds, we’ll tailor the PO layout to match their workflow.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Hi Vanessa —

Appreciate the summary and attachments. Quick clarifying Qs from procurement: 

- Procurement says a 36-month commitment will need VP Finance signoff and legal review — they typically allow 5–7 business days for a standard PO but have pushed back when vendor T&Cs deviate.
- They asked whether Redwood requires any non-standard indemnities or data retention clauses for the private offer (we didn’t sign those today).
- Also asked if AWS Marketplace can surface a single-line item for amortization — their ERP team prefers a fixed monthly charge vs a large lump-sum invoice.

I’m looping procurement on this mail so they see the materials; Procurement — could you confirm the approver list and whether some of these items (indemnity/data retention) will trigger legal escalation? If yes, we can target an approval window of 10 business days; otherwise, 3–5.

Thanks,
Nina
Director of Product, FinApps
Nina.Patel@finapps.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace AM <aws-am@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals & term options

Vanessa / Karthik —

Quick internal note for Nina and procurement: here is what Redwood typically does and what we need to keep the buyer approval path frictionless. 

1) Legal/ops on long-term private offers: 
- For 36-month POs we do require a standard long-term addendum to the Marketplace PO (simple clause: termination for convenience with 60 days notice, standard liability cap tied to fees paid). No unusual indemnity language normally.
- If the buyer requests custom data retention or data processing clauses beyond our SOC2 + standard DPA, that triggers legal review (typically 3–5 business days).

2) Billing/amortization: 
- AWS Marketplace supports monthly subscription billing for private offers if configured as a recurring charge. We can structure the PO as a monthly amortized charge against a single private offer ID — will require coordination with the AWS AM to set that up on their side.

3) Suggested buyer PO wording (short):
- "Redwood Inference — AWS Marketplace Private Offer PO #<finapps-po-number> — Term: 36 months — Recurring monthly charges per attached pricing grid. Standard Redwood Marketplace terms apply as attached."

4) Timeline expectations: 
- If procurement keeps to standard approval workflows and no custom legal clauses are requested, we can close in 3–7 business days. If legal redlines appear, add 5–10 business days.

Karthik — can you confirm whether we need CISO approval for the private offer record when the platform will be hosted in AWS and data residency is in us-east-1? Nina — tagging so procurement can confirm if they need that on file.

— Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@finapps.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finapps.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, AWS Marketplace AM <aws-am@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals & term options

Thanks all — quick operational checklist from Redwood to help procurement map approvals and avoid delays: 

- Buyer provides PO number and approver list (name, title, email).
- Confirm preferred invoicing cadence (monthly amortized vs annual upfront). If monthly, we'll request AWS AM to enable recurring billing on the private offer record.
- Confirm whether buyer needs a distinct billing entity or if the Marketplace invoice to FinApps is acceptable.
- If >24 months, Redwood requires an internal signoff (legal + finance). We’ve pre-authorized the standard 36-month addendum language Sergio pasted above — no extra redlines needed in typical cases.
- Security: If FinApps requires any additional SOC2 artifacts beyond the standard package we can supply them; CISO signoff is only required if custom processing clauses are requested.

Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Nina / Procurement to share the approver list and PO number by EOD Friday (2026-08-06).
2) Redwood to prepare Marketplace private offer record and send draft to AWS AM for recurring billing setup (ETA 48 hours after we receive approver list).
3) Procurement to confirm if legal redlines are needed; otherwise target approval within 3–7 business days once PO is lodged.

I’m attaching the short pricing grid and term sheet for reference (same doc Vanessa shared). I’ll be the internal owner to expedite legal/finance signoff on our side.

— Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-aws-po-term-sheet-v1.pdf, pricing-grid-annual-vs-36mo.xlsx
